correctness.rationale: For B_n signed permutation matrices U, the Schur-orthogonal coefficient embedding sends the reflection-matrix block to Mat_n with √n normalization. The adjoint-conjugation action on Mat_n splits multiplicity-free as scalar I (dim1), traceless diagonal (n−1), symmetric off-diagonal and skew off-diagonal (each n(n−1)/2). For a signed cycle type with f=f_++f_− fixed coordinates, s=f_+−f_− and τ=t_+−t_−, the squared projection energies of U are s²/n, f−s²/n, (n−f)/2+τ, (n−f)/2−τ, totaling n. Conjugacy averaging by sector Schur gives claimed w-scaled four eigenvalues including multiplicities. Solving equality of all four eigenvalues to w yields f=1,τ=0, and strictly positive levels yield the specified injectivity criterion: s≠0 and a long cycle or both 2-cycle signs. Checked the branch n=3 has no tight classes, n≥4 examples. Independently enumerated all 10 rank-three and all 20 rank-four signed conjugacy types and evaluated every basis vector of all four exact rational orbit operators; all agree, distinct from source’s rank-3-to-5 checker.
residual_risks: Multiplicity-free decomposition and cycle count conventions must not be interchanged with unsigned S_n or ordinary character-average normalization.
The finite n=3,4 enumeration corroborates but does not prove universal n.

value.rationale: The reflected-permutation group is a canonical Weyl type-B family, and restriction to a single conjugacy class is a natural exact sampling/identifiability question. The complete all-class eigenvalue census compresses to signed 1/2-cycle statistics and settles both frame tightness and Fourier block injectivity in all ranks; sign-sensitive obstructions provide structural information beyond an arbitrary finite computation.
residual_risks: Uses well-known Schur and irreducible sector theory; independent value rests on the explicit signed-cycle classification, not rebranding those tools.

scientific_limitations: Single conjugacy class only; no union-of-classes or other irreducible Fourier block claims.
